newsitem.title: UK: MEPC cancels swaps in cost-cutting drive.
newsitem.headline: MEPC cancels swaps in cost-cutting drive.

text.p: British real estate group MEPC Plc pushed its rationalisation plans one step further on Monday, after it cancelled some interest rate swap agreements to cut its sterling financing costs.

MEPC, which recently ended talks on a possible merger with rival Hammerson Plc and last week announced it would outsource the management of 340 properties, said the move eventually would enable it to improve dividend cover and earnings per share.

"This move resets the ratio of our fixed to floating rate debt at a more appropriate level and will substantially reduce our future costs. It will ensure our property decisions are not constrained by an artificially high cost of finance," chief executive James Tuckey said in a statement.

MEPC, one of Britain's leading property development and management companies, said it had written the interest rate swap agreements in the late 1980s or early 1990s to fix the effective cost of its sterling debt.
But the move meant MEPC's funding costs were now higher than its competitors, the company said. Newly-appointed finance director James Dundas said MEPC had been constrained by those costs.

MEPC said the cancellations would cut its overall effective interest cost by around 1.5 percent but that it would take a 73.2 million pound ($119.6 million) exceptional charge for 1997. Pre-tax profit before exceptional items would rise by nine million pounds in the second half.
The exceptional charge would drag earnings per share down by 11.7p but lower financing costs would result in a smaller net reduction of 10.2p, MEPC said.

MEPC said earnings per share were expected to benefit from the cancellations. For 1998 and 1999, earnings per share were expected to benefit by 3p and 2.5p respectively and pre-tax profits to rise by 19 million stg and 16 million respectively.
In addition, dividend cover was likely to improve from 1998 onwards. For 1997, the company pledged an unchanged dividend of 20p per share.
MEPC has benefited from improving conditions in the property market. Last December it reported annual pretax profits of 140 million pounds compared with 122.6 million a year earlier.

However, its net asset value per share dropped to 450p from 457p at the end of the previous year because of a writedown on a Los Angeles shopping mall. The group is targeting a NAV of 690 pence per share for 2001. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
